boards.school_name: South Dakota School of Mines and Technology
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented South Dakota Mines rituals, heritage objects, and recurring campus events—from M Hill to commencement.

cards.title: M-Day
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Mines homecoming tradition
cards.notes: Look for M-Day and Rocker Days announcements before planning a visit; the tradition began when the M was built on M Hill in 1912.
cards.short_summary: A homecoming-linked tradition anchored by the large M on M Hill.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines identifies M-Day as a time-honored tradition and dates its first observance to October 5, 1912, when the M was constructed on M Hill.
cards.source_title: Journey Through Time: History and Traditions Explored
cards.access_notes: Event details vary by year; consult the university’s current Rocker Days schedule.

cards.title: Freshman Beanies
cards.subtitle: Incoming-student rite of passage
cards.notes: Notice the green-and-yellow beanies during orientation season, and treat them as a campus welcome tradition rather than a visitor souvenir.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students have worn beanies at Mines since 1920.
cards.evidence_claim: The university states that each incoming freshman at South Dakota Mines has donned a beanie since 1920 and describes it as a freshman rite of passage.
cards.source_title: Journey Through Time: History and Traditions Explored
cards.access_notes: This is part of incoming-student orientation; participation is arranged by the university.

cards.title: Walk Through the Arch for Beanies
cards.subtitle: Orientation procession at Memorial Arch and Plaza
cards.notes: During fall orientation, watch for the cohort procession from the Surbeck Center to the quad, ending with beanies and the school song.
cards.short_summary: A newer orientation ritual pairs the historic Arch with the beanie tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines says that beginning in 2019, incoming freshmen are ushered from the Surbeck Center to the quad, walk through the Arch, receive beanies, and learn the school song.
cards.source_title: Journey Through Time: History and Traditions Explored
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of student orientation; public viewing and timing depend on the current orientation schedule.

cards.title: Whitewash the M
cards.subtitle: Annual upkeep of the M Hill monogram
cards.notes: View the M from campus or public streets; do not attempt hillside work or access closed terrain without university direction.
cards.short_summary: Students annually whitewash the M as part of the school’s M Hill tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines alumni materials describe students whitewashing the M each year as homage to the work associated with completing a Mines degree.
cards.source_title: The Arch: Annual Report of the Center for Alumni Relations and Advancement
cards.access_notes: Observe from designated public or campus areas; hillside maintenance is not a self-guided activity.

cards.title: Meet Grubby
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Mines mascot tradition
cards.notes: Find the campus Grubby statue for a documented visual marker of Mines spirit, and check athletics or campus events for mascot appearances.
cards.short_summary: The current mascot carries a history reaching back to a 1959 M-Day reference.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines reports that the first evolution of Grubby appeared in its 1959 student newspaper and that a bronze Grubby statue has been displayed on campus since 2011.
cards.source_title: New South Dakota Mines Mascot Design Unveiled
cards.access_notes: The statue is a campus landmark; event appearances depend on current athletics and campus schedules.

cards.title: The Commencement Mace
cards.subtitle: Faculty-chair procession at graduation
cards.notes: Look for commencement coverage or approved displays to see the mace; it begins the academic procession and includes Black Hills materials.
cards.short_summary: For two decades, this locally crafted mace has opened Mines commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The university states that its ceremonial mace has marked the start of commencement for two decades and is carried by the faculty chair in the academic procession.
cards.source_title: A Tradition Carried Forward: Ceremonial Mace Marks 20-Year Tradition at South Dakota Mines Commencement
cards.access_notes: The mace is used in commencement and may be displayed only at university-designated times.

cards.title: Rocker Days
cards.subtitle: South Dakota Mines homecoming week
cards.notes: Use the annual schedule to choose a public event, such as the parade, M Hill picnic, pep rally, or football-game activities.
cards.short_summary: Mines’ homecoming program gathers alumni and students around a multi-day fall schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Dakota Mines alumni office lists Rocker Days events including a pep rally, bonfire, M Hill picnic, downtown parade, football tailgate, and football game.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled annually; some listed events, including the gala, may require registration or a ticket.

cards.entity_name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service
cards.title: MLK Day of Service
cards.subtitle: Annual student food-drive service day
cards.notes: Join only through the university’s current volunteer sign-up or visit a participating collection site during announced hours.
cards.short_summary: Student groups turn the January holiday into a recurring community food-drive effort.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines says student groups have observed its MLK Day of Service tradition for 16 years by collecting food and cash donations for Feeding South Dakota and the campus food pantry.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Mines Students Make Community Impact Through Annual Day of Service Tradition
cards.access_notes: Occurs around the January MLK Jr. holiday; volunteer locations and hours are announced for each year.

cards.entity_name: Mines India Club Diwali Festival of Lights
cards.title: Diwali Festival of Lights
cards.subtitle: Annual Surbeck Center cultural celebration
cards.notes: Watch the Mines India Club and university event calendar for the next program; past events included lamp-lighting, performances, food, henna, and fireworks.
cards.short_summary: A decades-running India Club celebration shared with the Rapid City community.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines described its 2025 Diwali Festival of Lights as the 36th annual event, organized by the Mines India Club at the Surbeck Center.
cards.source_title: Mines’ India Club Invites Community to Celebrate 36th Annual Diwali – Festival of Lights
cards.access_notes: The 2025 university announcement described the event as free; confirm the next event’s details before attending.

cards.title: Holi Celebration
cards.subtitle: Annual festival of colors at Mines
cards.notes: Wear clothing suitable for color powder and follow the current event guidance; the university has hosted the celebration for more than 35 years.
cards.short_summary: A long-running campus Holi brings students and the community together to welcome spring.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines reports that its Student India Club has hosted the Holi Celebration for more than 35 years and describes it as an anticipated annual campus tradition.
cards.source_title: The Colors of Spring: Mines Student India Organization Hosts Community Hindu Holi Celebration
cards.access_notes: The university described the 2026 celebration as free and open to the public; confirm future dates and location.
